# FrameAssembly

> A Domain-Specific Language (DSL) for writing deterministic network traffic to `.pcap` files.

## Overview
FrameAssembly compiles a custom networking DSL (with the `.fasm` extension) into reproducible PCAP files. It uses a strict, keyword-oriented syntax designed for both network engineers and security researchers.

## Architecture & Folder Structure
- `src/main.rs`: Entry point handling CLI execution and parsing arguments.
- `src/lexer.rs`: Zero-copy tokenizer built using `logos`.
- `src/parser.rs`: Combinator-based AST parser built using `winnow`.
- `src/ast.rs`: Abstract Syntax Tree definitions for `HostDef`, `FlowDef`, and `FrameStatement`.
- `src/pcap.rs`: Handles writing packets to PCAP format using `pcap-file`.
- `src/packet.rs` & `src/backend.rs`: Handles packet encapsulation (L2-L4) via `etherparse` and AST evaluation.
- `examples/`: Contains `.fasm` training data and reference scripts.

## Syntax Guide & Examples
The DSL defines `HOST`s, `FLOW`s, and `COMPILE` blocks. 

```frameassembly
// Define network endpoints
HOST example_server { IP 10.0.10.5 MAC aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:ff }
HOST example_nms { IP 10.0.10.100 }

// Define sequence of packet transmissions
FLOW tcp_handshake(client, server) {
    client -> server TCP SYN PAYLOAD "Hello" 
    client <- server TCP SYN ACK PAYLOAD "World"
    client -> server TCP ACK PAYLOAD "!" 
}

// Compile block to execute flows
COMPILE {
    LOOP 10 {
        tcp_handshake(example_server, example_nms)
    }
}
```

- [README.md](README.md) - Full documentation and syntax guide
- [src/lib.rs](src/lib.rs) - Crate root and module exports
- [src/ast.rs](src/ast.rs) - Core structural types of the DSL
- [demo.fasm](demo.fasm) - Primary demonstration script
